verdicts.note: Two independent sources: the 2026 statement promises 'meaningful property tax relief for hardworking homeowners' and describes his senior and homestead exemption advocacy [S1], and in 2019 he said 'We have fought for years' to raise the senior threshold [S3]. The relief he seeks comes through exemptions, not lower levies, so -1 rather than -2; medium fits.

The only restraint evidence is one self-description of a lean office ('keeping costs low', fewer FTEs) [S1]. That is an incumbent's efficiency claim more than a position on audit versus invest. The dossier's own S4 points the other way: in 2019 he pressed the council for added positions and warned of 'significant detrimental impacts' if they were denied. The direction is plausible, but the evidence is indirect and partly contrary, so low rather than medium.

Pamphlet-only, but the pamphlet is explicit: he lists no elected experience and makes an outsider case from 'real-world' market experience, 'not just computer models', against a 15-year incumbent [S1]. One clear source supports +2 at medium.
